clue.text: One keeps it in reserve

parts.note: someone aloof or reserved holds others at arm's length, keeping a gap between them

explanation.definitionFit: To keep your distance is the idiom for staying reserved and standoffish with other people.

clue.text: Is the affluence they enjoy is unmerited?

definitions.text: Is the affluence they enjoy is unmerited?

parts.words: Is the affluence they enjoy is unmerited?
parts.note: describes wealthy people who do no work for their wealth, a leisured class of the moneyed

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the class of wealthy people who live without working, so their affluence is unearned.

clue.text: Virtually directed at the camping fraternity

parts.note: something directed at a person is sent to them
campers are everyone sleeping under canvas, so all in tents

explanation.surface: Something seems almost aimed at people who go camping.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is read as a phrase, split as TO + ALL IN TENTS, describing whom the message is addressed to.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in effect or practically, the same as virtually.

clue.text: Slight difference of opinion?

parts.note: the surface suggests a small disagreement, but the phrase means a subtle shade of meaning

explanation.definitionFit: A subtle shade or slight variation in meaning or tone is exactly a small difference.

clue.text: Heard I'd watched

indicators.note: heard tells us the word I'd is spoken and we take what it sounds like

parts.note: the contraction of I would or I had

explanation.surface: Someone claims they overheard what was being looked at.
explanation.definitionFit: To have looked at something closely is a synonym of having watched it.

clue.text: One forced to share his time with another

definitions.text: One forced to share his time with another

parts.words: One forced to share his time with another
parts.note: time here is a prison sentence, served in a shared cell alongside a fellow inmate

explanation.definitionFit: A fellow prisoner sharing the same cell serves time alongside another inmate.

clue.text: With high explosive around I would take cover

indicators.note: around tells us the explosive's letters sit on either side of the contraction

parts.note: I would contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: With explosives all around, a person decides to shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal yourself is a synonym of taking cover.

clue.text: Is provocative when it appears in a stage presentation

indicators.note: appears in says the word it is placed inside the reworked letters
a presentation is a new arrangement of what is given, so the letters of a stage are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something is controversial when it turns up in a theatrical production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presentation' reads as a stage show but signals the anagram: it rearranges A STAGE into AGATES, and 'appears in' sets the word it inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up or provoke trouble is a synonym of being provocative.

clue.text: Lie dying perhaps and surrender

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters given might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A dying person lies down and gives up.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving way or submitting is a synonym of surrender, used as a noun.

clue.text: Turn pale guilty perhaps

indicators.note: turn means the letters of the word pale are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A defendant goes white when declared guilty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guilty perhaps' defines by example: guilty is one answer a defendant can give in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A defendant's formal answer in court, such as not guilty, is called this.

clue.text: An honour that has to be fought for

definitions.text: An honour that has to be fought for

parts.words: An honour that has to be fought for
parts.note: a boxing trophy awarded to British champions, won literally by fighting

explanation.walkthrough: The Lonsdale Belt is the championship belt of British professional boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: This British boxing championship trophy is won in the ring, so it is literally fought for.

clue.text: Top level operation

parts.note: an operation at the top of the body, on the head, which is also proverbially the hardest kind

explanation.definitionFit: Surgery on the head's contents is literally at the top and proverbially the most demanding work.

clue.text: Benefit is cut about a quarter

indicators.note: about says the cut word goes round the quarter

parts.note: something cut into parts is divided
N is north, one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A payout is reduced by about a quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: A share payout to investors is a financial benefit.

clue.text: Cord I twisted into a sort of column

indicators.note: twisted says the letters of cord and I are wound into a new order

explanation.surface: Some cord gets wound round a pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the classical Greek orders of architecture names a plain style of column.

clue.text: Mount framing an artist in his element

indicators.note: in places an artist inside the word for his element

parts.note: an artist's element or field is art
an gives the letter A
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A picture mount surrounds a painter who is in his element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'framing' only sets the scene: the mount frames the picture. RA (Royal Academician) is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount names a mountain, and this Turkish peak is where Noah's ark came to rest.

clue.text: Thaw breaking out don't you think

indicators.note: breaking out says the letters of thaw are broken up and set out again

explanation.surface: A thaw is beginning, wouldn't you agree?
explanation.definitionFit: A tag question tacked on to ask agreement, as in 'Fine day, what?', means 'don't you think'.

clue.text: Les Miserables — or The Turn of the Screw?

indicators.note: a turn of something twists it round, so the letters of the screw are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Two famous novel titles are set side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: The novel title The Turn of the Screw tempts a literary reading; 'Turn of' is the anagram signal on THE SCREW.
explanation.definitionFit: The French title of Hugo's novel translates as the wretched or miserable ones.

clue.text: Some overseas lines

indicators.note: some says only part of the word overseas is wanted

explanation.surface: A few lines of text arrive from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines of poetry are collectively called poetry or stanzas, the same thing.

clue.text: Determined not to be caught napping

definitions.text: Determined not to be caught napping

parts.words: Determined not to be caught napping
parts.note: describes someone keeping watch and staying alert

explanation.definitionFit: Being watchful and alert means never being caught off guard.

clue.text: They may be eaten slowly or bolted

definitions.text: They may be eaten slowly or bolted

parts.words: They may be eaten slowly or bolted
parts.note: bolted looks like gobbled food, but these are the fixings screwed onto bolts, as well as kernels you eat

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both edible kernels and the threaded fasteners that go on bolts.

clue.text: Swimmer upsets one young salmon in ten

indicators.note: in puts the turned pieces inside the number

parts.note: taken as the word ten

indicators.note: upsets in a down clue turns the pieces upside down, reading them backwards

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a parr is a young salmon

explanation.surface: A swimmer overturns a young fish in a pool of ten.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upsets' reads upward, making RRAPI, which then sits inside the number.
explanation.definitionFit: This freshwater turtle is a swimming reptile.

clue.text: Drink triple gum normally with one rum

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Drink triple gum normally with one rum': the answer is an anagram ('rum') of GGG + ONE, but 'gum normally' gives no clear tripled G as held; likely OCR garble, not found online
annotationWithheld.clue: Drink triple gum normally with one rum

clue.text: Draughts we hear in Tony's place in the country

indicators.note: we hear says the word for draughts is taken by its sound

parts.note: the game of draughts is called checkers in America

explanation.surface: Someone hears of draughts being played at a country house.
explanation.walkthrough: Chequers is the British Prime Minister's country residence; Tony is Tony Blair, PM when the puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prime Minister's official country residence would have been Blair's home outside London.

clue.text: A newspaper leader

parts.note: a leader is also an opinion column, but this is the person who heads a paper

explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a newspaper heads its staff and decides its content.

clue.text: Nasty comedown for highway travellers

parts.note: the highway is the sky, so these travellers are air passengers and the comedown is a forced landing

explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's violent emergency touchdown is a literal and unpleasant coming down.

clue.text: A number set up as allies

indicators.note: set up in a down clue lifts the word upward, so it reads backwards

parts.note: six is a number

explanation.surface: One numeral is arranged as a group of partners.
explanation.definitionFit: The wartime alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan was known by this name, so it names a group of allies.

clue.text: Awkward ones voting negatively

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase describing the votes, a noun plural standing for those voting against

indicators.note: awkward means the letters of ones are put into a clumsy new order

explanation.definitionFit: Votes against a motion in Parliament are counted as the opposite of ayes.

clue.text: Some theorems Pythagoras had to observe

indicators.note: some says only a stretch of the words theories Pythagoras is wanted

explanation.surface: A geometry student must look at a few of the Greek's theorems.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, 'Some' hides MSPY, not ESPY, in 'theorems Pythagoras'; the setter evidently meant a word ending in E before the S, such as 'theories'.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch sight of or spot something is a synonym of observe.

clue.text: The height of distinction

definitions.meaning: a high piece of ground or elevation
fame or high rank and importance

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a raised place on the land and a high standing or renown.

clue.text: Watering plants is always in season

indicators.note: in places always inside the season

parts.note: spring is a season
ay is an old word for always

explanation.surface: Gardeners water plants regularly throughout the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying a fine mist of water to plants is how one waters them with a hose or can.
